mutant.description: Three mutants, each removing one step of my own method and re-running it, to test whether that step is load-bearing or decorative. Mutant 1 removes cohort-matching from the ETF delta. Mutant 2 removes name-normalization from the Cottonwood 18-strategy reconciliation. Mutant 3 takes Andrew's 'first available info' literally for the ETF Float, starting at the 2026-06-08 feed onset instead of the 2026-07-20 completeness date.
mutant.expected: Mutant 1 should inflate ETF growth by counting PFDE/PFOE's coverage onset as growth. Mutant 2 should manufacture false missing-strategy findings from cosmetic roster-name differences. Mutant 3 should inflate the float by subtracting an incomplete Cottonwood subtrahend at the start.
mutant.observed: MUTANT 1 FIRED: +$374,593,187.70 (+98.55%) mutated vs +$116,824,145.70 (+30.74%) correct; divergence $257,769,042.00, 2.2x apart. MUTANT 2 FIRED harder than predicted: exact-string matching reports 4 of the 18 as not-found ('Anna *9238', 'Moderate Income Portfolio', 'Opal - Beecherl Legg', 'Opal - Income') when all four are present; I predicted 1-2, measured 4, and corrected the deliverable to the measured figure. MUTANT 3 FIRED AND INVERTED THE SIGN, which makes it the most serious of the three: float delta reads +$657,896,761.38 mutated vs -$5,173,664.49 correct -- a $5.2M decline rendered as a $658M increase. Cottonwood's ETF-ownership feed carries 5 accounts / $194,520.46 at its 2026-06-08 onset vs 309 accounts / $52,007,438.70 at the end, with a 5->293 account jump in the week of 2026-07-08..07-15; and 2026-06-08 carries no netassets partition at all, so the mutated gross reads $0.00. Mutant 3 is the reading a careful person gets by following the instruction literally, which is why it was worth building.
